sentiment.label: risk_off
sentiment.reason_it: Il sentiment di mercato è risk-off a causa della guerra in corso tra Israele e Iran, con un impatto negativo sui mercati azionari e un aumento della domanda di asset rifugio. Il VIX è sceso a 18.05, ma rimane sopra la soglia di 15, indicando una certa incertezza. L'S&P 500 è salito dello 0.80%, ma il DXY è aumentato dello 0.07%, segnalando una certa avversione al rischio. Il prezzo del petrolio è salito dell'1.72%, raggiungendo $96.56 al barile, a causa delle tensioni geopolitiche.
sentiment.reason_en: Market sentiment is risk-off due to the ongoing war between Israel and Iran, with a negative impact on equity markets and increased demand for safe-haven assets. The VIX declined to 18.05, but remains above the 15 threshold, indicating some uncertainty. The S&P 500 rose 0.80%, but the DXY increased 0.07%, signaling some risk aversion. Oil prices rose 1.72% to $96.56 per barrel due to geopolitical tensions.

market_impact_summary.it: La guerra in corso tra Israele e Iran ha causato un aumento del prezzo del petrolio e una certa avversione al rischio sui mercati. L'S&P 500 è salito dello 0.80%, mentre il DXY è aumentato dello 0.07%. Il VIX è sceso a 18.05. Il TLT è sceso dello 0.44%, segnalando una certa pressione sui tassi. L'oro è salito dello 0.68%, raggiungendo $4832.60 l'oncia.
market_impact_summary.en: The ongoing war between Israel and Iran led to an increase in oil prices and some risk aversion in markets. The S&P 500 rose 0.80%, while the DXY increased 0.07%. The VIX declined to 18.05. The TLT fell 0.44%, signaling some pressure on interest rates. Gold rose 0.68% to $4832.60 per ounce.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno e benvenuti all'aggiornamento finanziario di oggi, il vostro Morning Briefing quotidiano.

I mercati asiatici hanno chiuso la giornata con un tono positivo. Il Nikkei ha guadagnato il 2.4% a 59,518, mentre lo Shanghai ha registrato un aumento dello 0.7% a 4100. L'Hang Seng di Hong Kong ha chiuso in rialzo dell'1.7% a 26,399. Questi dati potrebbero anticipare un'apertura positiva per i mercati europei.

L'S&P 500 ha chiuso con un guadagno dello 0.8% a 7000. Il Dollar Index (DXY) è salito dello 0.1% a 98. Il VIX, indice di volatilità, è sceso dello 0.7% a 18. I tassi di interesse continuano a essere sotto attenzione: il tasso decennale USA è salito al 4.3% con un incremento dello 0.6%. L'oro ha guadagnato lo 0.7% a $4800 l'oncia. Il mercato continua a monitorare l'evoluzione delle tensioni geopolitiche e i dati economici in arrivo.

Sul fronte geopolitico, la situazione rimane tesa. La crescita economica della Cina ha raggiunto il 5% nonostante le tensioni con l'Iran. Un membro della Fed ha avvertito che gli istituti di credito devono affrontare il 'doppio pericolo' rappresentato dalla guerra in Iran e dalle tariffe commerciali. Il Fondo Monetario Internazionale ha inoltre raccomandato all'UE di attenersi alle regole fiscali durante la crisi energetica.

In ambito macroeconomico, gli Stati Uniti attendono la pubblicazione del PIL del primo trimestre, prevista per il 29 aprile. La BCE ha recentemente mantenuto i tassi di interesse invariati, con il tasso sui depositi al 2%. L'inflazione nell'Eurozona è attesa per il 2 aprile. La liquidità globale, misurata dal Global M2, continua a espandersi con un aumento del 4.9% su base annua.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali...

Iniziamo con Bitcoin. Il prezzo attuale è di 74.631 dollari, con un aumento dell'1%. I flussi ETF hanno registrato un afflusso netto di 411 milioni di dollari. Tecnicamente, il supporto inferiore è stato testato, ma gli analisti ritengono che i mercati stiano ignorando una questione chiave legata all'Iran. La capitalizzazione di Bitcoin potrebbe crescere 'probabilmente molto più grande' del mercato dell'oro da oltre 30.000 miliardi di dollari.

Passiamo alle altcoin. Ethereum è attualmente a 2.339 dollari, con un aumento dello 0,8%. Solana guadagna il 2,6% a 85 dollari, mentre Binance Coin (BNB) sale dell'1,7% a 622 dollari. Solo il 4% dei cittadini danesi detiene criptovalute, un valore notevolmente inferiore rispetto ad altri paesi europei.

L'indice Fear & Greed è a 23, in zona di Extreme Fear. Il sentiment degli investitori sembra essere influenzato dalle notizie geopolitiche, come la situazione tra Iran e Israele. Gli afflussi record nei prodotti di investimento in Bitcoin, come ad esempio quelli che hanno raggiunto 2,7 miliardi di dollari in 48 ore, potrebbero indicare un cambio di tendenza nel breve termine.

In sintesi, il mercato delle criptovalute sembra essere in attesa di sviluppi macroeconomici e geopolitici. L'interesse per Bitcoin e le altre criptovalute rimane alto, con investitori istituzionali e individuali che continuano a monitorare l'evoluzione del settore.

Grazie per aver ascoltato il nostro podcast finanziario. Per domani, tenete d'occhio l'andamento dei mercati europei e americani, e monitorate le notizie relative alle decisioni delle banche centrali. Un saluto da Prais Alért, e a domani!
audio_script_en:
Welcome to your daily morning market briefing.

Global sentiment is risk-off today, as indicated by the mixed performance in Asian markets and a cautious tone in early European trading. The Nikkei and Hang Seng indices saw gains, but the Shanghai Composite edged up modestly. US futures suggest a slightly positive open, but overall, investors seem to be adopting a wait-and-see approach amid geopolitical tensions.

In traditional markets, equities are showing a mixed picture. At the last close, the S&P 500 index rose by 0.8%, while the STOXX 600 edged up 0.2%. The VIX index, a gauge of market volatility, slipped 0.7% to 18. In the currency markets, the EUR/USD pair weakened to 1.2, down 0.1% on the day. The Dollar Index (DXY) firmed up 0.1% to 98. Commodities are mostly higher, with Brent crude oil up 1.7% to $97 and gold prices rising 0.7% to $4800/oz. Bond yields are also on the move, with the US 10-year yield up 0.6% to 4.3%, while the TLT Bond USA 20Y slipped 0.4% to 87.

On the macro front, attention is focused on the ongoing earnings season and key economic data releases. In the US, recent data releases have shown a mixed picture, with inflation still a concern. The CPI and Core CPI YoY rates were last reported at 3.3% and 2.7%, respectively. The Federal Reserve's stance on interest rates remains a key market driver. Meanwhile, in the Eurozone, the focus is on the upcoming CPI and GDP growth data. Geopolitically, tensions in the Middle East and the ongoing trade tensions between the US and China are keeping investors on edge. Key events to watch include any developments in the Iran-Israel conflict and the US-China trade negotiations.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. Starting with Bitcoin, it's been a wild ride. The recent influx of $411 million into BTC ETFs has certainly caught attention. Currently, Bitcoin is trading at $74,631, up 1% from the previous day. Some analysts believe Bitcoin could grow significantly, potentially surpassing the $30 trillion gold market. However, with the current geopolitical tensions, particularly between Iran and Israel, Bitcoin's role as a 'digital gold' is being reevaluated. It's now being seen more as a geopolitical settlement bet rather than just a store of value.

Moving on to altcoins, we're seeing a mix of movements. Ethereum is up 0.8% at $2,339, while Solana has gained 2.6% to reach $85. Binance Coin is also in the green, up 1.7% at $622. The overall market sentiment seems to be cautiously optimistic, but it's essential to keep in mind that the Fear & Greed Index is currently at 23, indicating extreme fear.

Speaking of sentiment, the Fear & Greed Index at 23 suggests that investors are extremely fearful, which could be a sign of a potential buying opportunity. However, it's crucial to consider various factors before making any investment decisions. With the current market conditions and geopolitical tensions, it's essential to stay informed and up-to-date on the latest developments.

Thanks for tuning in, and we'll see you tomorrow. A final word from Prais Alért. Have a great day and we'll be back with more market insights soon. Goodbye.

articles.title: Implementing the digital euro project
articles.snippet: The European Central Bank (ECB) is working on a digital version of the euro, a project started back in 2020 that is coming closer to fruition as the enabling EU legislation progresses. The ECB has designed a digital equivalent of cash, aimed at complementing physical euros for day-to-day payments. Its approach may be compared and contrasted with the US Federal Reserve’s reluctance to introduce a digital dollar and with the People’s Bank of China’s definition of the digital yuan largely as a bank deposit. articles.title: Silent Killers, Not Signals: Why States Use Poison in Assassinations
articles.snippet: The recent news that Russian opposition leader Alexei Navalny’s death was caused by epibatidine — a South American frog toxin — has reignited interest in state use of poisons and toxins in assassinations. articles.title: Rethinking Security Cooperation in the Age of Commercial Tech
articles.snippet: Commercial technologies are enabling the U.S. military and militaries around the world to operate with greater efficiency, speed, precision, and lethality. The benefits of commercial capabilities can be particularly impactful given the defense industrial base’s struggles to produce at the speed and scale needed to outmatch China, Russia, and other aligned adversaries. It is largely for these reasons that President Donald Trump mandated the Department of Defense to preference commercial solutions. articles.title: The End of Managed Escalation in the Gulf
articles.snippet: The U.S.-Israeli war against Iran has exposed a reality many policymakers long preferred to avoid: The deterrence model that governed the Gulf for decades is no longer working as intended.For years, the region operated in the gray zone — covert strikes, proxy warfare, and carefully managed escalation. Iran built a strategy around missiles, regional partners, and nuclear latency.The United States underwrote Gulf security without direct war. Saudi Arabia and its neighbors relied on that umbrella while hedging against its limits, investing in missile defense and selective partnerships. There were rules, even if unwritten.That world is breaking down. The two-week ceasefire announced The post The End of Managed Escalation in the Gulf appeared first on War on the Rocks .

articles.title: IMF Warns Of Potential Global Recession Amid High Oil Prices
articles.snippet: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has cut its economic outlook for the world economy and warned it could sink into a recession if the Iran war is not soon resolved. In its April 2026 World Economic Outlook, the Bretton Woods institution has predicted that global GDP will expand by 3.1% in the current year, down from its earlier projection of 3.4%, if the conflict is short-lived and oil prices soon normalize to around $82 per barrel. articles.title: U.S. Is Most Resilient to the Energy Shock, Until It Isn’t
articles.snippet: The seven-week-long war in Iran has shown that the regions are not equally hurt by the worst oil and gas disruption in history. Asian countries, which are most dependent on oil and LNG flows from the Middle East, are already grappling with fuel shortages, airlines are raising fares and grounding flights, and refiners bid for every non-Middle Eastern barrel in a fierce competition to procure crude. That’s true for most of Asia, but not for China. Beijing has been amassing crude into commercial and strategic storage over the past year—at…

articles.title: Norway’s Oil Export Earnings Surge 68% Amid Iran War
articles.snippet: Norway's crude oil export earnings surged 67.9% year-on-year in March to a record 57.4 billion kroner ($6.1 billion), primarily driven by soaring global energy prices following the outbreak of the Iran war and the subsequent closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Oil prices averaged 1,014 kroner ($107.52) per barrel in March, the highest monthly average since September 2023. As Europe’s largest producer of oil and natural gas, the Scandinavian country exported 56.6 million barrels of crude oil in March, good for nearly 2 million barrels per day.…

articles.summary_it: Norway's crude oil export earnings surged 67.9% year-on-year in March to a record 57.4 billion kroner ($6.1 billion), primarily driven by soaring global energy prices following the outbreak of the Iran war and the subsequent closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Oil prices averaged 1,014 kroner ($107.52) per barrel in March, the highest monthly average since September 2023. As Europe’s largest producer of oil and natural gas, the Scandinavian country exported 56.6 million barrels of crude oil in March, good for nearly 2 million barrels per day.…

articles.title: Bitcoin Price Passes $75,000 as Iran War Turns It From ‘Digital Gold’ Into Geopolitical Settlement Bet
articles.snippet: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Passes $75,000 as Iran War Turns It From ‘Digital Gold’ Into Geopolitical Settlement Bet Bitcoin price jumped past $75,000 on Wednesday as traders recalibrated what the asset represents in the wake of the Iran conflict and an unusually stretched derivatives market. articles.title: Oil’s 50% Surge Sparks Supercycle Talk but Risks Linger
articles.snippet: Oil prices are up by over 50% since the end of February, ready for further gains should the situation in the Middle East deteriorate again. Supply is tight and getting tighter by the day. A fifth of global LNG supply is offline. The energy sector is once again hot, and commentators are talking about a new supercycle. Investors rushing to oil and gas stocks would be unsurprising, but perhaps some caution is advisable. articles.title: European Buyers Eye Canadian LNG to Diversify Supply
articles.snippet: European energy companies are eyeing purchases of Canadian liquefied natural gas in search of supply diversification in challenging times, according to a Reuters report citing unnamed sources familiar with the matter. European energy buyers are already big clients of U.S. LNG producers, but long-term diversification would require spreading reliance over more suppliers, hence the interest in Canadian LNG, which has yet to start flowing. The report concerned a planned LNG export terminal, Ksi Lisim, which has yet to get a final approval and move…
